validated_results.title: Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Green Tea Catechins for Prostate Cancer Prevention.
validated_results.reason: This is a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial investigating the effect of green tea catechins on incident prostate cancer in men with high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia or atypical small acinar proliferation.

extraction.comparison_type: Polyphenon E (400 mg EGCG/day) vs placebo
extraction.population: Men with high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) and/or atypical small acinar proliferation (ASAP)

sample_size.excerpt: Summary of Toxicities by Final Attribution and Treatment Arm - All Patients (N=97)

cases.excerpt: Among the men with ASAP at baseline, 2/17 in the PolyE arm versus 4/14 in the placebo arm were subsequently diagnosed with PCa over the 12 month study. Among the 10 cancers diagnosed on the 12-month biopsy, no significant effect of the intervention on tumor grade could be detected.

p_value.excerpt: No differences in the number of PCa cases were observed: 5/49 (PolyE) versus 9/48 (placebo), P=0.25.

comparison.excerpt: Forty-nine participants were randomized to the PolyE arm and 48 to the placebo arm, with 70 completing the 12-month intervention and 74 reaching the primary endpoint, with at least a 6 month biopsy.

design.excerpt: We conducted a placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial of Polyphenon E® (PolyE), a proprietary mixture of GTCs, containing 400 mg (–)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) per day, in 97 men with high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) and/or atypical small acinar proliferation (ASAP).

timing.excerpt: The primary study endpoint was a comparison of the cumulative one-year PCa rates on the two study arms.

continent.excerpt: Participants were enrolled at the Moffitt Cancer Center, James A. Haley VA Hospital, Tampa and University of Florida, Jacksonville, Florida from September 2008– March 2013.
continent.location: Materials and Methods, Eligibility and recruitment, Paragraph 1

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Polyphenon E™ (PolyE), an investigational agent manufactured by Mitsui Norin Co., Ltd., Shizuoka, Japan, was used in this clinical trial. The active pharmaceutical ingredient of PolyE is a purified tea fraction containing 80% to 98% total catechins by weight; the main component of which is EGCG, comprising 50% to 75% of the material.
